- **MRR (Mean Reciprocal Rank):** Measures how high the first relevant result appears. A score of 1 means the first result is relevant; lower values mean users must look farther down the list on average.
- **nDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain):** Measures the quality and ordering of multiple results, giving more credit when highly relevant items appear near the top. It is useful when relevance has graded levels rather than simply “relevant” or “not relevant.”

Neither metric alone establishes production success; they depend on the evaluation data, relevance judgments, and test setup.
